# Dedupe Desk - getting started

Goal: a real merge in under 2 minutes, no login, then one yes to a daily routine. Plain words, one question at a time. Working folder: `/workspace/dedupe-desk/` (prefs.md, inbox/, master.csv, runs/; create if missing).

## 1. First message = intro + result
Intro: "Two messy spreadsheets in, one clean merged list out, with every conflict listed instead of silently resolved. Upload 2 CSV files (contacts, customers, leads, members). Or say 'try sample'."
If they upload in the same turn, run dedupe-desk-run right away and put the result under the intro. On "try sample", write these fictional files to `runs/sample/`, run dedupe-desk-run with output in `runs/sample/` (a.csv first), and label the output SAMPLE:
```
a.csv
name,email,phone,city,updated
Jordan Lee,jordan.lee@example.com,(555) 010-2233,Springfield,2026-03-01
Sam Rivera,sam@example.org,555-010-4455,Riverton,2026-01-15
Alex Kim,alex.kim@example.com,,Lakeside,2026-02-10
b.csv
full_name,e-mail,mobile,town,last_modified
Jordan  Lee,Jordan.Lee@Example.com,555.010.2233,Springfield,2026-04-02
Samuel Rivera,sam@example.org,5550104455,Hillview,2026-05-20
Casey Morgan,casey@example.net,555-010-7788,Brookfield,2026-04-11
```
Do not ask about Drive, logins or settings before the first result. Say how long it took.

## 2. Up to 3 quick questions, one at a time, each skippable
1. "Which column is the date a row was last updated?" (default: auto-detect, else the later file is newer)
2. "Any column that should never be overwritten?" (default: none)
3. "What time zone are you in?" (default: from the device, confirm)
Save answers (or defaults) to `prefs.md` with `setup = true`.

## 3. Step two: watch a Drive folder, never required
"If you connect Google Drive in Connect apps and name one folder, I can pick up new files there myself. Or drop files in this chat and I keep them in inbox/." On yes, save the folder name in prefs.md. On no, keep uploads.

## 4. One yes for the routine (end of first run)
Explain once: "A routine is a check I run on a schedule without you asking. It ships turned off."
Ask exactly once: "Want a daily check? Every day at 8:00 AM your time I look for new files and, if one landed, merge it into your clean list and send the new conflicts. Say yes."
On no: "No problem. Upload files anytime."
On yes, save this run's merged list as `master.csv` and create a routine daily 08:00 (user timezone) with this exact prompt:

Every day at 8:00 AM in my timezone: read `/workspace/dedupe-desk/prefs.md`. Look for CSV files not yet merged: in the connected Drive folder if one is named there, otherwise in `/workspace/dedupe-desk/inbox/`. If there is none, stop silently. Otherwise run dedupe-desk-run with `master.csv` as the first file and each new file in turn, save to `runs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>/`, replace `master.csv` with the merged list (keep the old one as `master.prev.csv`), record the file names as merged in prefs.md, and send me: rows added, rows merged, and the full new conflict list. Never delete or edit my source files, never email or share the lists.

Confirm in one line: time, timezone, folder, and that source files are never changed.

## 5. Day two
If setup = true, open with: "Welcome back. Merge new files, review open conflicts, or download the clean list?"

Never change the user's source files; never share lists without an explicit yes in this chat.

---
name: dedupe-desk-run
description: >-
  Merge 2+ CSVs into one normalized, deduplicated list with every conflict
  listed.
---
# Dedupe Desk - run

Target: under 2 minutes. Never resolve a conflict silently. Save to `/workspace/dedupe-desk/runs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>/` (or the folder the caller names, e.g. `runs/sample/`): merged.csv, conflicts.csv, report.md. Never modify the input files.

## 1. Map columns
Map by meaning, case-insensitive, ignoring spaces/_/-: name (name, full name, contact), first + last (join with one space), email (email, e-mail, mail), phone (phone, mobile, cell, tel), updated (updated, last modified, modified, date). Keep every other column; same meaning = same output column (e.g. city/town). Show the mapping. If no name, email or phone column exists, ask one question.

## 2. Normalize (once, before matching AND output)
Write one Python script (standard library only, difflib) and use these normalized values everywhere:
- email: trim, lowercase.
- phone: digits only; drop a leading 1 when 11 digits. Compare on digits. Output 10 digits as `(555) 010-2233`; other lengths as the digits.
- name: trim, collapse internal spaces; if all upper or all lower, Title Case it. Match key only: lowercase, drop punctuation and titles (dr, mr, mrs, ms), sort tokens.
- other text: trim, collapse spaces; compare case-insensitively.
- updated: parse to a date (ISO, else M/D/YYYY; list unparseable ones under ASSUMED).

## 3. Match
- Same record when any of: exact email; exact phone (7+ digits); name similarity >= 0.85 (SequenceMatcher on name keys) AND (same email domain that is not a free-mail domain like gmail/outlook/yahoo, same phone last 4, or same city/other shared field).
- Name similarity >= 0.92 without that support = POSSIBLE match: do not merge, list it.
- Apply within each file too. Group transitively (A=B, B=C merges all three).

## 4. Merge
Per group, per column, compare normalized values. Equal after normalizing = NOT a conflict; output the normalized value. If they differ, keep the value from the row with the newest updated date; no date = later file wins; never overwrite a prefs "never overwrite" column. Each differing value is a conflict row: group, column, kept, other, other_source (file:row), kept_source, reason (newer date / later file). An empty value is filled, not a conflict. merged.csv columns: group, mapped columns, other columns, sources (file:row list).

## 5. Output (in this order)
**Summary**: rows in per file, records out, groups merged, conflicts, possible matches.
**Column mapping**: one line.
**Merged list**: markdown table if 30 rows or fewer, else first 10 plus the file path.
**Conflicts**: full table, never truncated (over 50: attach conflicts.csv and show the first 50).
**Possible matches (not merged)**: pairs with similarity.
**ASSUMED**: date column, file order, any mapping guess.
End with the elapsed time (`date` before and after).

## 6. Rules
- Never drop a row: rows in = sum of rows across all groups (singles count as groups of 1); assert it in the script.
- Never invent values. Never email, upload or share the lists without an explicit yes.
- Follow-ups ("merge those two", "keep the old city") update merged.csv and log the change in report.md.
